- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 3–8% for next 5–10 days.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.1) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for 3–7 day horizon.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above recent 10d average, reduce by 1–3% for next 5 days.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 5+ consecutive days), apply 2–5% downward adjustment to next forecast.
- If sentiment history shows sudden shift from negative to positive (e.g., 0.0 → 1.0), model often overreacts; dampen forecast by 3–7% for 2–5 days.
